description: Evolution of architectural styles, structures, and key architects through history

ancient_architecture.mesopotamian: Ziggurats; stepped mud-brick towers (Temple of Ur)
ancient_architecture.egyptian: Pyramids, obelisks, massive temples; limestone and granite; Giza Pyramid (c. 2560 BCE)

orders.corinthian: Elaborate acanthus leaf capital; widespread in Rome

byzantine.key_works: Hagia Sophia (537 CE, Istanbul); cross-in-square church plans

romanesque.characteristics: Rounded arches, thick walls, small windows, barrel vaults

baroque.characteristics: Dramatic movement, curved forms, elaborate ornamentation

modern_architecture.neoclassicism: 18th–19th century revival of Greek/Roman forms; US Capitol, Panthéon Paris
modern_architecture.art_nouveau: 1890–1910; organic forms, flowing lines; Gaudí (Sagrada Família, Park Güell)

bauhaus.founded: 1919 by Walter Gropius in Weimar, Germany
bauhaus.principles: Combine craft and fine art; 'form follows function'

international_style.characteristics: Steel, concrete, glass; minimal ornamentation; open floor plans

postmodernism.characteristics: Eclectic mix of styles; historical references; wit and irony

iconic_structures.sydney_opera_house: Sydney; 1973; Jørn Utzon; shell roof design
iconic_structures.sagrada_familia: Barcelona; Gaudí; under construction since 1882; expected completion 2026
